title: Shabads close
hook: births, weddings, deaths, days: the Granth sings through them all

segments.voice: Yesterday, aukhad, and your line: sing it for them. Today this whole stretch of shabads for a life closes, seen from end to end.

One family, one long life. A baby comes home, and a grandfather sings. Twenty-five years later, the same child walks four slow rounds around the Guru Granth Sahib. There are hospital nights, a move across an ocean, a new house blessed. And one day, the family gathers to sing for that same person one last time. Through all of it, someone is singing: mostly from the Guru Granth Sahib, sometimes from the Tenth Guru's own writings. For thirty-five days, this path has followed that life. Today: shabad.
screen: `A BABY COMES HOME.` → `FOUR ROUNDS, A NEW HOUSE.` → `ONE LAST SONG.`

segments.voice: Look back at the turns. Birth: Guru Arjan's joy when his son Hargobind was born, a gift arriving. Marriage: the four laavan of Guru Ram Das, dharma, fearless, longing and union, and before them the palla placed in the bride's hand while the hem of the Lord is sung. Protection: the hot wind that doesn't touch, and the Guru's hand over your head. Neighbors: hukam, one Lord behind every name. Loss: the Tenth Guru's song to the beloved Friend from the forest, and Guru Nanak's laments, which open with blessed and remember that all must go. Courage: subh karman, never turn from good, and sooraa, accepted in His court. Then the ordinary days: dukh bhanjan, the ragi choosing the right song, two lines learned by heart, a hymn sung for a friend. Two of those, the song to the Friend and grant me this, come from the Dasam Granth, the writings linked to the Tenth Guru; the rest are in the Guru Granth Sahib. Add it up. The Guru Granth Sahib isn't only read on special occasions. It's built to meet every turn of a life. Sikhs say the Guru is present in the shabad, so at each turn the Guru is there too: at the cradle, at the wedding, at the bedside, at the cremation. A Sikh family doesn't need to invent words for the big moments. They're already written, and already sung. And you don't need to know all of them. A handful, really known, can carry a life.
screen: `BIRTH, MARRIAGE, PROTECTION.` · `NEIGHBORS, LOSS, COURAGE.` · `THE ORDINARY DAYS.` · `THE GURU AT EVERY TURN.` · then, large: `A HYMN FOR EVERY TURN.`

segments.voice: Go slowly through the turns of a life: a birth, a wedding, a hard night, a loss, an ordinary morning. For each one, let a line from this path come to mind, the one you'd want sung then, and count them on your fingers, one to five; the meaning is enough, not the exact words. If you pray, you can say Waheguru after the fifth.
Shabad, a hymn from the Guru Granth Sahib, sung for every turn of a life: births, weddings, protection, loss, courage and ordinary days, the Granth singing through them all.
Your line: a hymn for every turn. Thirty-five days of them, and the Guru at each one. See you tomorrow.
